messages:
carla (support): FYI customer ACME opened ticket #4721, reporting a sudden p95/p99 spike after last night's continuous-batcher canary. Short prompts spiking to ~1.0-1.3s p99, p95 ~250-420ms. They also noticed a tiny fraction of 401s during the window.

mike (eng-sre): Which change was promoted in the canary? Any batching param tweaks?

jen (eng-platform): We rolled continuous-batcher v2.3.1 at 02:12 UTC. Change log: batch_timeout_ms increased 15 -> 35 to boost throughput for midsize requests. Rollout finished by 02:46 (deploy-bot).

deploy-bot: rollout complete continuous-batcher v2.3.1 -> 100% (1799991000)

ash (oncall): Infra graphs show tiny prompts are accumulating in the coalescer. Sample from gpu-58: 
```
[2025-11-22T02:33:08Z] req=acme-rt1 prompt_tokens=6 BatchWaitMs=39 serve_ms=1210
[2025-11-22T02:33:09Z] req=acme-rt2 prompt_tokens=3 BatchWaitMs=37 serve_ms=1168
```

carla (support): I replayed a subset of their traffic and can reproduce p99 rise when batch_timeout_ms >= 30ms. p50 stable. Also hit ~0.12% 401s during high hold times.

mike (eng-sre): Sounds like the classic timeout vs throughput tradeoff; increasing batch_timeout raises batching efficiency but worsens tail for sparse small requests. Do we have auth logs for the 401s?

kevin (security): Pulled auth logs. There is a burst of token validation errors aligned with the same interval. Upstream token refresh seems to produce ephemeral headers that are considered valid for ~28ms; if requests are held longer than that, retries can hit 401s.

jen (eng-platform): Current tenant-level config that got applied: 
```
batch_timeout_ms: 35
max_batch_size: 64
grace_window_ms: 8
adaptive_coalesce: false
```

tom (product): Reverting the global change would help ACME but might regress throughput for many tenants. Per-tenant override seems preferable.

mike (eng-sre): Agreed. Fast mitigation: hotpatch ACME to batch_timeout_ms=12 and enable adaptive_coalesce so tiny prompts are short-circuited. Also add small random jitter to coalesce wait to avoid synchronized expiry races.

ash (oncall): Applying tenant override now.

ash (oncall): action: tenant_override set tenant=acme {batch_timeout_ms:12, adaptive_coalesce:true} -> OK

ash (oncall): Metrics after override: ACME p99 dropped from ~1.2s -> ~200ms within 60s. p95 down to ~80ms. Customer confirmed recovery in the ticket.

carla (support): Customer message: 'Latency is back to normal, thanks for the quick fix' :tada: 

mike (eng-sre): Good. Follow-up actions: 
- Add an automated rollback rule: if tenant p99 jumps >500ms within 10m of a batcher rollout, auto-pin to prior config and alert SRE.
- Create a unit/integration test that simulates token TTL vs batch hold to catch auth races in CI.
- Implement per-tenant short-prompt ratio heuristic to choose lower batch_timeout or adaptive_coalesce by default.
- Add jitter to batch wait windows to break synchrony with ephemeral token TTLs.

kevin (security): I'll instrument token refresh latency and add an alert that correlates auth failures with BatchWaitMs > 25ms. Also will audit any other short-lived header paths that could be impacted.

jen (eng-platform): Opening a rollback PR to revert the global batch_timeout bump until we have tenant-aware rollout heuristics + canary gating based on short-prompt ratios. Adding console UI for per-tenant overrides and a note in onboarding docs for chatty tenants.

mike (eng-sre): Also note: add a smoke test to canary that replays a 1k-request short-prompt distribution to validate no p99 regressions before global promotion.

ash (oncall): Drafting post-incident note with timeline, hotpatch commands, sample logs and graphs. Will include playbook entry for per-tenant overrides.

tom (product): Please cc CS on the postmortem and include recommended defaults: 'if >40% of requests <12 tokens, use batch_timeout <=15ms or enable adaptive_coalesce'.

sre-bot: Incident INC-4721 resolved. Mitigation verified, customer acked.

carla (support): Closing ticket; will file follow-ups for docs and console flags.

(emoji reactions: :white_check_mark: on ash, :heart: on mike)
